userStories.title: Expose flow stop detail, feature branches and thread filtering
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the existing flow response and project list with the already-persisted stop detail, feature branches and optional thread filter.

**Motivation** — A flow that stops or asks a question notifies the user, but the notification has nowhere to send them.

**Approach** — The flow DTO gains only fields its record already carries: `stopDetail` on the flow and `branch` on each feature. `FleetFlowRecord` and the flow repository's include are unchanged.

The thread filter adds `threadId` to the `findPage` filters only when it is set (`{ projectId, ...(threadId ? { threadId } : {}) }`), so a list call without it passes the same filters as today.

`FleetFlowDto` (`apps/api/src/fleet/flows/dto/fleet-flow.dto.ts`): Target: `stopDetail: string | null` (`@ApiPropertyOptional({ type: String, nullable: true })`), from `record.stopDetail ?? null`. `FleetFlowFeatureDto` (same file): Target: `branch: string | null`, from `feature.branch ?? null`. Follow the existing nullable Swagger annotation pattern for branch.

`ProjectFlowsController.list`: Target: `list(rawQuery: ListFleetFlowsQuery, ctx)`; `ListFleetFlowsQuery extends KodaPageQuery` adds `threadId?: string` (`@IsOptional() @IsString() @MaxLength(64)`). It parses with `parseQuery(ListFleetFlowsQuery, rawQuery)` (which drops undeclared keys, so the class must be the new one) and calls `this.flows.list(ctx.project.id, { current, size }, { threadId })` with the parsed `threadId`. Add optional Swagger query metadata and retain default paging.

`FleetFlowsService.list`: Target: `list(projectId, page, filters: { threadId?: string } = {})` calls `this.flows.findPage({ projectId, ...(filters.threadId ? { threadId: filters.threadId } : {}) }, page)`. `PrismaFleetFlowRepository.findPage` and `IFleetFlowRepository.findPage`: Target: `findPage(filters: { projectId: string; threadId?: string }, page)`; when `threadId` is set the `where` adds `threadId`. Existing project scope, newest-first order and feature ordering are preserved.

Extend DTO exact-object expectations with only the new nullable keys; extend fleet-flow-read-stop.spec.ts for controller/service delegation, existing repository integration tests for thread isolation, and the endpoint e2e flows block using its `newThread` helper. Regenerate `openapi.json` from the root with `bun run api:export-spec`; do not hand-edit generated artifacts. Query validation must reject a 65-character threadId with HTTP 400.

**Scope** — In: additive DTO serialization, optional query, repository interface/implementation filter and associated unit/DB/endpoint behavior. Out: overview readers/route (US-002/003), web DTOs and panel (US-004/010), changes to create/stop/answer routes. Changing any flow step, state transition or stop rule in the API.

**Interface**
```ts
class ListFleetFlowsQuery extends KodaPageQuery {
  @IsOptional() @IsString() @MaxLength(64)
  threadId?: string
}
// FleetFlowsService
list(projectId, page, filters: { threadId?: string } = {})
// IFleetFlowRepository and PrismaFleetFlowRepository
findPage(filters: { projectId: string; threadId?: string }, page)
```

userStories.title: Define web flow contracts and pure view helpers
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add hand-written web flow DTO types and pure helpers shared by the composable, pages and sections.

**Motivation** — The flow DTO already carries a `url` field that names this page (`fleet-flow.dto.ts`, "the web path F6 renders"), and the web app has no route for it.

**Approach** — `lib/fleet-flows.ts` holds the DTO types and the pure helpers named in Design. Mirror the serialized FleetFlowDto, FleetFlowFeatureDto (including branch), FleetFlowQuestionDto, FleetFlowPage and overview/job/repo shapes, including approval, stopDetail, nullable questions/answers and ISO timestamps. Reuse ApprovalRequestSummary from lib/approval-requests.ts rather than redefining it. Do not introduce a generated web client or browser-side money aggregation.

PR links are built in the web app from the overview's repo: `https://github.com/<owner>/<name>/pull/<n>` when `provider` is `github`; any other provider, or no overview, shows `#<n>` without a link.

A feature's branch is `feature.branch` when set, else the flow's `branch` (feature 1 keeps the flow branch).

Flow jobs. Jobs with no feature are shown in a "Flow jobs" section after the features, only when there are any. `jobsByFeature` returns an entry (possibly empty) for every feature. Group by feature name, preserving input order; null-feature rows go into flowJobs.

Stop and Answer go through the existing gated routes. Either may answer 202 with an approval request summary; the page tells the user an approval was requested and links to `/:project/approvals`. The pending check is the `useProviderCredentials` pattern (`'permissionKey' in data`). Make the helper safe for non-object/null input.

States and steps render through literal maps in `lib/fleet-flows.ts` from the code to an i18n key, with the raw code as the fallback for an unknown value: `flowStateKey` (`fleet.flows.state.<code>`: `PENDING`, `APPROVED`, `RUNNING`, `WAITING_MERGE`, `WAITING_ANSWER`, `COMPLETED`, `STOPPED`), `featureStateKey` (`fleet.flows.featureState.<code>`: `PENDING`, `RUNNING`, `WAITING_ANSWER`, `READY`, `MERGED`, `COMPLETED`, `STOPPED`) and `flowStepKey` (`fleet.flows.step.<code>`: `SPEC_REVIEW`, `PLAN`, `PRD_REVIEW`, `RUN`, `REVIEW`, `RULE`, `FIX`). The three groups are registered in the locale parity spec's `ENUMS`. Registration and locale strings are delivered by US-006; this story implements literal-map helpers with null for unknown/null codes. LIVE_FLOW_STATES contains only PENDING, APPROVED, RUNNING, WAITING_MERGE, WAITING_ANSWER. openQuestions returns questions only while answeredAt is null and questions exists. Add tests in tests/lib/fleet-flows.spec.ts.

**Scope** — In: DTO mirrors, FlowRepo, pure liveness/label/branch/PR/grouping/questions/pending-discriminant helpers. Out: HTTP wrapper (US-005), locale registration and page rendering (US-006/007), action UI (US-008/009). PR links for providers other than GitHub; a non-GitHub repo shows the PR number without a link.

**Interface**
```ts
// apps/web/lib/fleet-flows.ts
export const LIVE_FLOW_STATES: readonly string[]      // PENDING APPROVED RUNNING WAITING_MERGE WAITING_ANSWER
export function isLiveFlow(state: string): boolean
export function flowStateKey(state: string): string | null   // literal map to fleet.flows.state.<code>, null if unknown
export function featureBranch(flow: FleetFlowDto, feature: FleetFlowFeatureDto): string
export function prUrl(repo: FlowRepo | null, prNumber: number | null): string | null
export function jobsByFeature(jobs: FleetFlowJobDto[], features: FleetFlowFeatureDto[]): { byFeature: Map<string, FleetFlowJobDto[]>; flowJobs: FleetFlowJobDto[] }
export function openQuestions(feature: FleetFlowFeatureDto): FleetFlowQuestionDto[]
export function isPendingFlowAnswer(data: unknown): data is ApprovalRequestSummary
```
Also export featureStateKey(state: string): string | null and flowStepKey(step: string | null): string | null, as required by the literal-map design and criteria.

userStories.title: Wrap project flow reads and gated writes in useFleetFlows
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the thin Nuxt API composable used by all flow screens and actions.

**Motivation** — A flow that stops or asks a question notifies the user, but the notification has nowhere to send them.

**Approach** — `composables/useFleetFlows.ts` wraps the five calls through `useApi()`: `list` (`?current=&size=20`, plus `threadId` when given), `get`, `overview`, `stop` and `answer`, the last two returning `FlowWrite`. Return typed API data unchanged for reads. Use /projects/<slug>/flows paths, because useApi already supplies the /api base, envelope unwrapping, locale, SSR cookie forwarding and auth handling. Encode path/query values without changing the concrete query order current, size, threadId. Do not swallow errors or add local business rules/state.

Stop and Answer go through the existing gated routes. Either may answer 202 with an approval request summary; the page tells the user an approval was requested and links to `/:project/approvals`. The pending check is the `useProviderCredentials` pattern (`'permissionKey' in data`). Delegate body discrimination to isPendingFlowAnswer from US-004, returning pending rather than treating an approval request as a saved flow. `stop` posts to /projects/:slug/flows/:flowId/stop. `answer` posts to /projects/:slug/flows/:flowId/answers with exactly { jobId, answers }. Unit tests mock useApi/$api in tests/composables/useFleetFlows.spec.ts.

**Scope** — In: typed list/get/overview/stop/answer calls and FlowWrite mapping. Out: page loading/error presentation (US-006/010), permission decisions, Stop/Answer form/toasts (US-008/009), polling (US-011).

**Interface**
```ts
// apps/web/composables/useFleetFlows.ts
export type FlowWrite = { kind: 'done'; flow: FleetFlowDto } | { kind: 'pending'; request: ApprovalRequestSummary }
export function useFleetFlows(slug: string): {
  list(page: number, threadId?: string): Promise<FleetFlowPage>
  get(flowId: string): Promise<FleetFlowDto>
  overview(flowId: string): Promise<FleetFlowOverviewDto>
  stop(flowId: string): Promise<FlowWrite>
  answer(flowId: string, jobId: string, answers: { id: string; answer: string }[]): Promise<FlowWrite>
}
```

userStories.title: Render the flow detail header, spend, approvals and stop context
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Create the flow detail page shell with independent flow/overview loading and complete header context.

**Motivation** — The flow DTO already carries a `url` field that names this page (`fleet-flow.dto.ts`, "the web path F6 renders"), and the web app has no route for it.

**Approach** — `pages/[project]/flows/[id].vue` loads the flow and its overview and renders the header: state, entry, branch, roles, created time, spend against cap with the unknown-cost line, the approval record, and the stop reason, stop detail and ticket link. It shows not-found and load-failed states. Strings come from `fleet.flows.*` keys in `en.json` and `zh.json`. Its tests live in `tests/pages/fleet-flow-detail.spec.ts`.

Agent-written text (questions, `stopDetail`, `stopReason`) renders through interpolation only, never `v-html` (`.nax/mono/apps/web/context.md`).

States and steps render through literal maps in `lib/fleet-flows.ts` from the code to an i18n key, with the raw code as the fallback for an unknown value: `flowStateKey` (`fleet.flows.state.<code>`: `PENDING`, `APPROVED`, `RUNNING`, `WAITING_MERGE`, `WAITING_ANSWER`, `COMPLETED`, `STOPPED`), `featureStateKey` (`fleet.flows.featureState.<code>`: `PENDING`, `RUNNING`, `WAITING_ANSWER`, `READY`, `MERGED`, `COMPLETED`, `STOPPED`) and `flowStepKey` (`fleet.flows.step.<code>`: `SPEC_REVIEW`, `PLAN`, `PRD_REVIEW`, `RUN`, `REVIEW`, `RULE`, `FIX`). The three groups are registered in the locale parity spec's `ENUMS`. Add all three translated groups now, even though the feature sections use the latter two in US-007. Existing locale keys and ENUMS entries stay unchanged.

Web test harness: pages and the panel import `useFleetFlows` explicitly (`import { useFleetFlows } from '~/composables/useFleetFlows'`), as `schedules/[id].vue` imports its composables, because `tests/helpers/mount-sfc.ts` injects only the Nuxt auto-imports it lists. Tests mock the composable by module path. `window.confirm` is stubbed on `globalThis.window`, as in the admin roles page tests. Confirmation belongs to US-008; retain this import seam from page creation.

On mount call get(flowId) and overview(flowId) once each; do not let overview rejection hide a successful flow. A first flow GET answering 404 shows fleet.flows.detail.notFound; other initial failures show fleet.flows.detail.loadFailed. Recognize ApiError.code 404 and the envelope 40004 convention. Overview is optional for the header; a failure keeps the flow and supports the jobsFailed fallback integrated in US-007. Use formatUsd(spentUsd) and formatUsd(costCapUsd); the positive unknownCostCount line reads `cap excludes N jobs with unknown cost` and is absent at zero. PENDING with approvalRequestId links to /:project/approvals; approved flows show approval mode, approver and recorded time. Load useProjectMemberNames(slug); name lookup failures are cosmetic and fall back to approverId itself. STOPPED displays literal stopReason/stopDetail and a ticket link /:project/tickets/<ticketRef> when overview supplies one. Preserve a reload function/event seam for dependent action stories. No polling is started in this story; US-011 owns its lifecycle.

**Scope** — In: page shell/loading/error/header/approval/stop-ticket rendering, initial shared locales and enum parity registration. Out: feature and job sections (US-007), Stop controls (US-008), answer forms and reload wiring (US-009), polling (US-011), breadcrumb/navigation changes (US-012). Approving or rejecting the flow's start request on the flow page; the page links to the existing approvals page.

**Interface** — Consume useFleetFlows(slug).get(flowId): Promise<FleetFlowDto> and overview(flowId): Promise<FleetFlowOverviewDto> from US-005, including overview repo, ticketRef, jobs, truncated and unknownCostCount. Use useProjectMemberNames(slug)'s { members, load, nameOf } and formatUsd(decimal) without recomputing money.

userStories.title: Show ordered feature progress, PRs and linked jobs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add ordered feature sections and feature/flow job lists to the detail page.

**Motivation** — The design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-04-fleet-flow-design.md`, G8 and "Status page") calls for a page that shows each feature's current step, its jobs, its PR and the cost against the cap.

**Approach** — `components/fleet/flows/FlowFeatureSection.vue`, rendered by the flow page once per feature in position order, shows the feature's name, state, current step, `dependsOn`, branch, PR link and its jobs. The page renders a "Flow jobs" section for jobs with no feature, when there are any. Section tests live in `tests/components/flow-feature-section.spec.ts`; page-level tests (ACs 1, 8, 9, 10) are added to `tests/pages/fleet-flow-detail.spec.ts`, created by US-006. The DTO is already position-ordered; keep its order rather than sorting alphabetically.

PR links are built in the web app from the overview's repo: `https://github.com/<owner>/<name>/pull/<n>` when `provider` is `github`; any other provider, or no overview, shows `#<n>` without a link.

A feature's branch is `feature.branch` when set, else the flow's `branch` (feature 1 keeps the flow branch).

Flow jobs. Jobs with no feature are shown in a "Flow jobs" section after the features, only when there are any. `jobsByFeature` returns an entry (possibly empty) for every feature.

`FlowFeatureSection` props: `slug`, `flow` (the flow DTO), `feature`, `repo` (the overview repo or null), `jobs` (that feature's jobs), `canAnswer` (the page's `permissions.value.has('fleet.flow.answer')`); it emits `answered`, re-emitted by its `FlowAnswerForm`. userStories.title: Poll live flow details with visibility-aware lifecycle control
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Keep a live flow's page current with bounded visibility-aware polling while retaining data on transient failures.

**Motivation** — F1-F5 built and verified the engine; live flows 13 and 14 were followed with SQL, `gh` and a polling script, because nothing in the web app shows a flow.

**Approach** — Live updates by polling use the existing `useVisiblePolling(task, 15_000)` (`composables/useVisiblePolling.ts`: one run at a time, a rejected run does not stop it, it pauses while the tab is hidden). The page starts it after the first successful load and calls `stop()` when the flow is no longer live or the page unmounts. The page re-reads the flow and its overview every 15 s while the flow is live (`PENDING`, `APPROVED`, `RUNNING`, `WAITING_MERGE`, `WAITING_ANSWER`), and stops polling once it is `COMPLETED` or `STOPPED`, when the first load fails, or when the page unmounts. No flow event exists on the project event stream, and adding one is out of scope.

A poll fails: the page keeps the data it shows and polls again at the next tick. Do not reset a successful flow view to the initial load-failed/not-found state on a polling rejection, including a rejected flow GET. Preserve the last successful overview when its polling read fails as well; continue trying both reads at subsequent ticks. A first flow GET failure, whether 404 or other, does not start a timer; a successful flow with only an overview failure remains live and may poll. Terminal state from a successful read stops the poll even if the overview read failed. Use the existing poller, not a second interval or SSE; do not modify its generic semantics. Guard asynchronous initial completion so leaving during the first load cannot start polling after unmount. US-008/009 reloads must not multiply timer registrations. Tests use fake timers in tests/pages/fleet-flow-polling.spec.ts.

**Scope** — In: detail-page poll setup/first-success start/live-state stop/cleanup, retained-data failure semantics and timer behavior. Out: initial header layout (US-006), job/feature rendering (US-007), mutation UI (US-008/009), thread/list polling, A flow event on the project event stream (SSE); the flow page polls every 15 s instead.

**Interface** — Consume useVisiblePolling(task: () => Promise<void>, ms: number), which returns { start, stop, runNow, isActive }; consume isLiveFlow(state: string): boolean and useFleetFlows(slug).get/overview for every refresh.

[unit] When a poll's get returns the flow as COMPLETED, advancing fake timers by another 15 s calls get no further time.
[unit] For a flow that is COMPLETED at the first load, advancing fake timers by 15 s calls get no second time.
[unit] After a failed first get, advancing fake timers by 15 s calls get no second time.
[unit] After the page unmounts, advancing fake timers by 15 s calls get no second time.
[unit] When a poll's get rejects, the page still renders the flow's branch, and the next 15 s tick calls get again.
